newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russia GDP to grow two percent in '97.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia GDP to grow two percent in '97.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said Russian Gross Domestic Product would grow at least two percent this year.
"This year for the first time growth of gross domestic product will reach at least two percent," Yeltsin said in an address to both houses of the parliament.
GDP fell six percent last year, confounding official hopes at the beginning of the year that 1996 would see the start of recovery.
GDP has fallen every year since Russia became independent with the break-up of the Soviet Union in 1991, and is now only 61 percent of 1991 levels, according to official statistics.
